title: A loop whose only work is creating objects holds memory far past the memory limit.
text: `while ($i < $n) { $head = new Node($head); $i = $i + 1; }` runs to its end under `nvs run` however much it holds: many millions of linked objects, several times the ceiling, and the memory-limit `FATAL` is raised only by the first `echo` after the loop, naming a reading well above the ceiling. A loop that throws and keeps every error as the next one's `previous` does the same. With no `echo` behind it and the list dropped, the program exits `0`, so a `while (true)` of this shape is bounded by the host and not by `[limits] memory`. An object is never refused: [`object::nvs_object_new`] allocates without [`budget::affords`], so the ceiling is held only by [`budget::carry`] raising `MEMORY_LIMIT` on the polled word for the loop's back-edge poll to read, and that poll does not report it. [`budget::carry`] raises nothing while the thread's ceiling is `0`, and its `publish` returns early while the polled word is null; which of the two holds under `nvs run`, or whether the compiled loop reads a different word, is not checked. `a-loop-that-only-concatenates-never-stops` is the same missing report seen through an allocation that is refused. The fix is owed to `tests/hostile/tools/php-differences/two-spellings-side-by-side/02-a-cart-that-grows-past-the-memory-limit.nvs`, which carries this record's marker.
